_comment_purpose: Tier 1 smoke test. Runs the ported WDL against microGWAS's own bundled small test dataset to confirm the DAG executes end-to-end and scatter logic resolves. This is a plumbing check, NOT a statistical one.
_comment_dataset: Unpack test/small_fastas.tgz and test/stripped_small_gffs.tgz from the microGWAS repo, then rebuild the full GFFs the way test/run_tests.sh does (concatenate each stripped GFF, '##FASTA', then the matching assembly). Paths below assume that has been done under tests/test_data/microgwas_small/.
_comment_lineages: The bundled genomes are too small for MLST to type, so upstream's own harness substitutes the canned test/lineages.txt. Passing it here as lineages_file skips the lineage_st task, matching that behaviour.
_comment_eggnog: Upstream's harness swaps the full Bacteria database (taxid 2) for Gammaproteobacteria (taxid 1236) to keep the download manageable. Better still: run the download once, park the tarball in GCS, and set eggnog_db_tarball instead.
_comment_covariates: Deliberately NOT set, even though test_data.tsv carries synthetic covariate1/covariate2 columns (6 and 7) and upstream's config documents '--use-covariates 6q 7' as the example. prepare_pyseer.py reduces the phenotype file to just the index plus the single target column before pyseer sees it, so 1-based columns 6 and 7 do not exist in the file pyseer is handed. Upstream never caught this because its CI only ever ran a Snakemake dry run. Confirm against a real run before relying on covariates; the Tier 2 E. coli dataset has no covariate columns, so this does not block validation.
